description: Somalia’s rich terrestrial and marine biodiversity forms a vital part of the Horn of Africa and East African Coastal Forests biodiversity hotspots. These ecosystems support food security, livelihoods, and climate resilience but are increasingly threatened by both exogenous and anthropogenic drivers of degradation including unregulated charcoal production, overgrazing, IUU fishing, agricultural encroachment, recurrent droughts, and conflict. Since the state collapse in 1991, formal protection and management of biodiversity and natural resources has been minimal, and most “protected areas” exist only as point records without mapped boundaries or active management and law enforcement.
